text: On the last night, while John was away in town, as soon as the moonlight came and that poor thing began to shake the pattern, I got up and ran to help her. <break time="0.8s" /> I pulled and she shook, I shook and she pulled, and before morning we had peeled off yards of that paper, a strip as high as my head. <break time="0.8s" /> I locked the door and threw the key down into the front path, for I did not want anybody to come in until John came home. <break time="0.8s" /> Now I creep smoothly around the room, for my shoulder just fits in that long smooch around the wall, so I cannot lose my way. <break time="0.8s" /> I do not like to look out of the windows, for there are so many creeping women outside, and I wonder whether they all came out of the wallpaper as I did. <break time="0.8s" /> When John came and found the door locked, he cried for an axe, but I told him in the gentlest voice that the key was by the front steps, under a plantain leaf. <break time="0.8s" /> He came in at last and stopped short by the door, but I kept on creeping just the same, looking at him over my shoulder. <break time="0.8s" /> I have got out at last, said I, in spite of you and Jane, and I have pulled off most of the paper, so you cannot put me back. <break time="0.8s" /> Now why should that man have fainted, I wondered, for he fell right across my path by the wall, so that I had to creep over him every time.
